prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Atlanta to replace my air conditioner?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t name a single “best” company for everyone — the right contractor depends on your zip code, home size, budget, timeline and whether you need ductwork or other repairs. If you tell me your zip code, the age/type of your current system, and roughly what you want (basic replacement vs high‑efficiency upgrade), I’ll shortlist 3–4 well‑rated Atlanta contractors and give a direct comparison.

Meanwhile, here’s a quick guide to help you choose the best HVAC company for replacing your air conditioner:

What to do next
- Get 3 written estimates from different contractors for the exact same scope of work.
- Ask each company to do a Manual J load calculation so the system is properly sized — don’t accept a “rule of thumb” sizing.
- Require a written contract that lists equipment make/model and SEER rating, labor warranty, permit handling, disposal of the old unit, and total price.

What to look for in a contractor
- Proper licensing and insurance (ask for license number and verify).
- EPA Section 608 certification (required to handle refrigerants).
- NATE‑certified technicians is a plus.
- Positive recent Google/Yelp/Angi reviews and a good BBB rating.
- Clear, itemized written estimate (equipment, labor, permit fees, taxes).
- Willingness to show references and explain load calc, ductwork needs, and warranty coverage.
- Offers permits and pulls them for you.

Questions to ask every contractor
- Will you perform a Manual J and show me the results?
- What exact model (brand and model number) are you proposing and why?
- What SEER rating and refrigerant does it use?
- What are the equipment and labor warranties? Is there a manufacturer warranty registration process?
- Do you include a permit and post‑install inspection?
- Do you recommend duct sealing or modifications?
- What is the installation timeline and payment schedule?

Typical cost ranges in Atlanta (very approximate)
- Basic replacement (older 13 SEER style, established house, no major ductwork): roughly $3,500–$6,000.
- Mid‑range (higher efficiency 15–17 SEER, some upgrades or minor ductwork): roughly $6,000–$10,000.
- High‑efficiency or complex installs (18+ SEER, mini‑split systems, major ductwork): $8,000–$15,000+.
Final price varies with tonnage, house size, difficulty of install, brand, and whether ductwork or electrical upgrades are needed.

Other tips
- Check for available rebates (Georgia Power, local utilities, and manufacturer rebates).
- Consider energy efficiency vs payback — a higher‑SEER unit saves more on energy bills but costs more up front.
- Ask about post‑install tuneups and maintenance plans.

If you want, give me:
- Your Atlanta zip code
- Size of house or number of tons (if known) or the model of your current system
- Any preferences (brand, budget, timeline, warranty needs)

I’ll find and compare 3–4 well‑rated local HVAC companies and summarize their pros/cons, typical estimate, and recent review highlights.
